criticalFindings.title: Workspace summary disagreement between protocol and formalization
criticalFindings.description: The protocol message indicates 'workspace: 1 accepted upstream revisions travel by content address' but the formalization JSON states 'workspaceSummary: 0 accepted upstream revisions travel by content address'. The task projection also shows 'upstream-accepted[0] sha256:745cadc1131468039f167043c000fc0af170ed98764f545f22d867be36da1c35 :: accepted revision of define-product-intent'. This fundamental disagreement about workspace state must be resolved before acceptance.

criticalFindings.impact: The formalization may be based on incorrect workspace assumptions. If there is actually 1 accepted upstream revision (sha256:745cadc1131468039f167043c000fc0af170ed98764f545f22d867be36da1c35), the entire formalization needs to account for this existing state and integrate it properly.

criticalFindings.title: Source claim digests don't match task projection
criticalFindings.description: The task projection specifies different source claim SHA256 digests than what appears in the formalization. Task projection shows claims with digests b15c35da..., cb291aa7..., 6652762b..., 3d576e96... but the formalization shows fbe292e8..., c9bfe922..., 423be112... This suggests either the wrong formalization is being reviewed or the task projection references different source material.
criticalFindings.impact: Cannot determine if the correct formalization is being reviewed. The source claim mismatch suggests either protocol error or wrong formalization version.

criticalFindings.title: Documented SHA256 digests don't match actual file content
criticalFindings.description: Every artifact file has a SHA256 digest in the formalization that does not match the actual file content. This violates CON-1 which requires content address transport with correct SHA256 digests.
criticalFindings.impact: Complete content address transport failure. Downstream components cannot verify intent integrity or resolve content to exact artifact states.

secondaryFindings.title: Trace relationships reference incorrect digests
secondaryFindings.description: Since all artifact digests are incorrect, the entire trace graph references non-existent content states. The trace shows '100% coverage' but this is meaningless when the references are wrong.
secondaryFindings.impact: The trace graph cannot be used for verification or dependency tracking when all digest references are incorrect.

secondaryFindings.title: Protocol message format may violate content address transport
secondaryFindings.description: The protocol message uses 'sha256:' prefixed hashes as artifact identifiers rather than pure content digests. This may indicate improper content address transport implementation.
secondaryFindings.impact: Protocol confusion about content address transport mechanics.

recommendation: REJECT formalization for complete resubmission. Multiple critical issues including workspace state disagreement, source claim mismatch, and content address integrity failures prevent meaningful review. The formalization must address these fundamental issues before acceptance.
reviewerNotes: This formalization cannot be properly reviewed due to multiple critical issues that suggest fundamental problems with either the task protocol, the formalization process, or both. The workspace summary disagreement (0 vs 1 upstream revisions), source claim digest mismatch between task projection and formalization, and complete content address integrity failure all indicate systemic issues that must be resolved at the protocol/formalization process level before individual desk formalizations can be properly evaluated.
